newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to help China in study to turn coal into oil.
newsitem.headline: Japan to help China in study to turn coal into oil.

text.p: Japan will help China with a feasibility study aimed at launching a plant to turn coal into light- and medium-grade oil, a Japanese Trade Ministry official said on Wednesday.
The three-year study is due to begin during the current 1997/98 fiscal year, the official said, adding Japan was waiting for China to name the area where it wanted the study to be made.
The study will include taking coal from the area and testing it at a new coal-into-oil plant in Japan.
The Japan International Cooperation Agency, the aid arm of the Foreign Ministry, will study the economic potential of the project, the Trade Ministry official said.
The basic agreement for the project was reached during talks in April, the official said, and will be signed once Beijing responds to the proposals.
He said it was unclear when China would respond or when the plant would be built.
Japan launched a prototype Japanese plant which processes coal into medium- and light-grade crudes in March.
The pilot plant in Ibaraki prefecture, northeast of Tokyo, can turn 150 tonnes of coal per day into roughly 600 barrels of oil.
